title: The Prince Who Never Became King

scenes.vo: He cost two hundred and twenty two million euros. The most expensive footballer in history.
He scored eighty goals for Brazil. More than Pelé.
He won the Champions League, and Olympic gold.
body: Neymar won the [[h2|Champions League]] with Barcelona in 2015, and captained Brazil to [[h3|Olympic gold]] in Rio a year later.

scenes.vo: And yet, he never won the Ballon Dor. He never won the World Cup. And when it ended, in tears, in July 2026, he said just two words. I tried.
scenes.pre: He never won the [[q0|Ballon d'Or]]. He never won the [[q1|World Cup]].

scenes.vo: This is the story of the prince who never became king.

scenes.title: The Boy from Mogi
scenes.vo: Chapter one. The boy from Mogi.
Neymar da Silva Santos Júnior was born on the fifth of February, 1992, in Mogi das Cruzes, near São Paulo. His father, Neymar senior, was a footballer whose own career never took off.
scenes.dek: A footballer's boy is born in [[f0|Mogi das Cruzes]]
body: Neymar da Silva Santos Júnior was born on February 5, 1992, near São Paulo.
His father, Neymar Sr., played professionally, but his [[f1|own career never took off]]. He would pour everything into his son.

scenes.vo: Brazil has always crowned its kings. Ronaldo, Rivaldo, Ronaldinho and Kaká all won the Ballon Dor. But after Kaká, in 2007, the crown was waiting for someone new.
scenes.title: Brazil's kings

scenes.vo: The family moved to the coast, and at eleven, the boy joined Santos. The club of Pelé.
He made his debut at seventeen. At nineteen, he led Santos to their first Copa Libertadores in nearly fifty years, and won FIFA's Puskás Award for goal of the year.
body: A teenage Neymar inspires Santos to their [[c0|first Copa Libertadores]] since the days of Pelé.
He also wins FIFA the [[c1|Puskás Award]] for the goal of the year.

scenes.vo: And he played with joy. The step-overs, the flicks, the celebrations. To millions of children, he was football.
scenes.text: To millions of children, he was football.

scenes.vo: Brazil had found its heir. The next Pelé. The crown prince of Brazilian football.

scenes.title: The Heir
scenes.vo: Chapter two. The heir.
In 2013, Barcelona signed him. That summer, he won the Golden Ball, as Brazil lifted the Confederations Cup.
The transfer would follow him for years. A Brazilian company claimed the true fee had been hidden. In 2022, a Spanish court cleared him of fraud and corruption.
body: A Brazilian firm claimed the [[c0|true fee was hidden]].
A Spanish court [[c1|clears Neymar]] of fraud and corruption over his 2013 transfer.

scenes.vo: Alongside Lionel Messi and Luis Suárez, he formed the most feared attack in the world. M. S. N.
body: Messi, Suárez and Neymar: [[c0|the most feared attack]] in world football.

scenes.vo: In 2015, they won the treble. Neymar scored in the Champions League final.
scenes.foot: Neymar [[h0|scored in the final]] as Barcelona beat Juventus 3–1.

cues.h0: scored in the Champions League final

scenes.vo: In 2017, Barcelona trailed Paris Saint-Germain four nil from the first leg. Neymar scored twice, and set up the winner, in a six one comeback.
body: Trailing [[c0|4–0 from the first leg]], Barcelona win 6–1.
Neymar [[c1|scores twice and sets up the winner]] in the final minutes.

scenes.vo: But there was a problem. He was playing beside Messi. Twice, he finished third for the Ballon Dor. As long as he stayed, he would always be the prince.
scenes.title: Ballon d'Or file
The Weight of a Nation
scenes.vo: Chapter three. The weight of a nation.
In 2014, Brazil hosted the World Cup. Neymar carried the nation, until a knee to the back in the quarter-final broke a vertebra.
body: Brazil's talisman is carried off against Colombia with a [[c0|broken vertebra]]. His tournament is over.

scenes.vo: Without him, Brazil lost seven one to Germany. The most humiliating night in their history.
scenes.foot: [[h0|The most humiliating night]] in Brazil's history.

scenes.vo: Two years later, at the Rio Olympics, he scored the winning penalty, to give Brazil its first ever Olympic gold in men's football.
body: Captain Neymar scores the [[c0|winning penalty]] against Germany: Brazil's [[c1|first Olympic gold]] in men's football.

scenes.title: The €222 Million Gamble
scenes.vo: Chapter four. The two hundred and twenty two million euro gamble.
In August 2017, Paris Saint-Germain paid his release clause. Two hundred and twenty two million euros. More than double the previous world record.
scenes.note: [[m0|More than double]] the old world record

scenes.vo: The plan was simple. Leave Messi's shadow. Win the Champions League. Win the Ballon Dor.
Then, his body began to break. A broken metatarsal in 2018. Another in 2019. An ankle injury cost him the Copa América, which Brazil won without him.
scenes.title: Medical file: Neymar Jr.
rows: Ankle: misses Copa América. [[r2|Brazil win it without him]]

scenes.vo: At the 2018 World Cup, he became a meme, mocked around the world for rolling on the floor. Brazil went out to Belgium in the quarter-finals.
body: Neymar's theatrics turn him into [[c0|a global meme]].
Brazil fall to Belgium in the [[c1|quarter-finals]].

scenes.vo: In 2019, he tried to go back to Barcelona. The deal never happened, and some PSG fans turned against him.
scenes.title: Transfer file: summer 2019

scenes.vo: In 2020, he finally reached the Champions League final. PSG lost one nil, to Bayern Munich.
body: PSG reach their [[c0|first Champions League final]], but Bayern Munich win [[c1|1–0]].

scenes.title: So Close
scenes.vo: Chapter five. So close.
At the 2022 World Cup, against Croatia, he scored a stunning goal in extra time. His seventy seventh for Brazil. Level with Pelé.
body: A brilliant [[c0|extra-time goal]] against Croatia: Neymar's 77th for Brazil, [[c1|level with Pelé]].

scenes.vo: Minutes later, Croatia equalised. Brazil lost on penalties. Neymar was due to take the fifth. He never kicked a ball.
In 2023, he passed Pelé, to become Brazil's all-time top scorer.
scenes.foot: Neymar [[h0|passes Pelé]] on FIFA's official count.

scenes.title: The Road Home
scenes.vo: Chapter six. The road home.
That summer, he joined Al-Hilal in Saudi Arabia, for a reported ninety million euros. Two months later, playing for Brazil, he tore his ACL.
In January 2025, he went home to Santos. Injuries followed him there too. But he helped his old club avoid relegation.

Then came one final chance. Carlo Ancelotti named him in Brazil's 2026 World Cup squad. A calf injury limited him to two games. In the round of sixteen, Erling Haaland scored twice, and Norway knocked Brazil out.
body: Picked by Ancelotti despite fitness doubts, a [[c0|calf injury]] limits Neymar to two games.

scenes.vo: Neymar scored a late penalty. His eightieth goal for Brazil. Afterwards, in tears, he said his Brazil career was over. I tried.
scenes.pre: His [[q0|80th goal]] for Brazil. His last.

scenes.title: The Verdict
scenes.vo: Chapter seven. The verdict.
Eighty goals for Brazil. A Champions League. Olympic gold. Twice third in the Ballon Dor.
So what went wrong? Some blame the injuries. Some blame the move to Paris. Some say he loved the spotlight more than the work. The truth is probably all three.
By any normal standard, a legendary career. But Neymar was never measured by normal standards. He was measured against Messi, Ronaldo, and Pelé. And next to kings, a prince will always look small.
scenes.text: Next to kings, a prince looks small.

scenes.vo: So, was Neymar a failure, or a legend? Tell me in the comments. And subscribe, for the next story.
